public_rationale: Before June 2024, GPT-4 on its own was weak at open-ended autonomous building. The SWE-bench paper found frontier models, GPT-4 included, could fix only the simplest real GitHub issues, with the best model under 2%. Aschenbrenner's own essay puts GPT-4 alone at about 2% on SWE-bench, rising only with Devin's scaffolding. The strongest counterexample, Coscientist (Nature, December 2023), was a human-built tool system driven by GPT-4 that optimised known reactions. It was not GPT-4 doing original work on its own. Read plainly, with 'on its own' and the 'as far as I know' hedge, the claim holds.
limitations: The verdict depends on excluding scaffolded systems like Coscientist and Devin.
Proving no case existed is not possible; the claim is hedged to Marcus's knowledge.

statement.excerpt: Smart high schoolers often do original work, like competing for science fair prizes with original ideas or designing and implementing original computer systems singlehandedly. GPT-4 on its own ain’t doing any of that, as far as I know.

from_speaker: original work, like competing for science fair prizes with original ideas
designing and implementing original computer systems singlehandedly
our_interpretation: Read as a claim that, as of the post date, there was no documented case of GPT-4 by itself (without a human-built tool system steering it) producing original science-fair-level research or singlehandedly building an original computer system.
Systems where humans wrap GPT-4 in tools and automation do not count as 'on its own', but they are noted as context.
Benchmarks of autonomous software work are used as a proxy for 'designing and implementing computer systems singlehandedly'.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations up to June 2024 show GPT-4 alone failing at autonomous, open-ended software or research tasks, and no documented case shows it doing original work of this kind unaided.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented case before June 2024 shows GPT-4 alone producing original research ideas carried through to results, or singlehandedly designing and building an original software system.
